summary: Segment Routing steers packets using a list of segments, and this works with the MPLS data plane. This document extends MPLS LSP ping and traceroute so they can test and trace paths for IGP-Prefix and IGP-Adjacency segment identifiers.

eli5.summary: Ping and traceroute check whether a path works. This teaches them to check paths made of segment instructions.

questions: how to ping a segment routing path
what is an igp adjacency segment id
how does lsp traceroute work with segment routing
subtitle: Teaching MPLS ping and traceroute to test paths that are built from Segment Routing segments.

tldr.problem: Segment Routing steers packets with a stack of segment IDs that are not always assigned hop by hop. A faulty node can send a packet the wrong way and still have it arrive, so ordinary MPLS ping and traceroute may miss the fault.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8287 adds three Target FEC Stack sub-TLVs (types 34, 35 and 36) for IPv4 prefix, IPv6 prefix and adjacency segment IDs, plus rules for how responders check them and how initiators build and trim the FEC stack.
tldr.outcome: LSP Ping and Traceroute from RFC 8029 can now validate IGP-Prefix and IGP-Adjacency SIDs on an MPLS data plane. RFC 8690 and RFC 9214 update this document.

today: RFC 8287 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 8690 and RFC 9214, so read those alongside it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 8029 defines MPLS "echo request" and "echo reply" messages for finding data-plane failures in Label Switched Paths (LSPs). Modeled on ICMP echo (RFC 792), the functions are usually called LSP Ping and LSP Traceroute.

The Segment Routing (SR) architecture uses source routing: a node steers a packet through a set of instructions called segments by prepending an SR header. On an MPLS data plane the SID is 20 bits and the SR header is the label stack, so the mechanics of RFC 8029 can be applied directly.

The difference from LDP or RSVP is that a Segment ID is not always assigned hop by hop. Depending on its type, it can be unique to a node or within a domain. That raises extra questions about fault detection and isolation, and this document defines LSP Ping and Traceroute for SR IGP-Prefix and IGP-Adjacency SIDs.
sections.eli5: Ping and traceroute check whether a road works. Segment routing writes the route as a list of stops, so the checkers need new ways to read those stops.

sections.title: Why Existing Tools Fall Short
sections.content:
The RFC gives an example network of eight routers, R1 to R8, with Node Segment IDs 5001 to 5008. Adjacency Segment IDs include 9124 (R2 to R4) and two for parallel links between R3 and R6: 9136 over link L1 and 9236 over link L2. An Adjacency Segment ID means "pop this ID and send the packet to a specific neighbor over a specific link".

A malfunctioning node may use it to forward to the wrong neighbor or over the wrong link. If R1 sends a stack of {9124, 5008} and R2 is misprogrammed to send the packet to R1 or R3, the packet may still reach R8 when the nodes share the same SR Global Block, but not by the expected path.

Traceroute may catch that deviation. The RFC then gives a case where it may not: R3 forwarding a packet with Adjacency Segment ID 9236 over L1 instead of L2.
sections.eli5: If a signpost says "take the left bridge" and a mistaken guide sends you over the right bridge, you might still get to town, but not the way the map said. You need a check that notices which bridge you used.

sections.title: The Segment ID Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
Three new sub-TLVs go into the Target FEC Stack TLV (Type 1), the Reverse-Path Target FEC Stack TLV (Type 16) and the Reply Path TLV (Type 21): 34 IPv4 IGP-Prefix Segment ID, 35 IPv6 IGP-Prefix Segment ID and 36 IGP-Adjacency Segment ID. Each describes the FEC for one label in the stack, which lets Ping and Traceroute work even when the responder sees fewer labels than the Target FEC Stack has FECs.

The prefix sub-TLVs carry the prefix, a one-octet Prefix Length (1 to 32 for IPv4, 1 to 128 for IPv6), a Protocol field and a Reserved field that MUST be 0 on send and ignored on receipt. For Protocol, 1 means the responder MUST validate using OSPF, 2 means IS-IS, and 0 lets it use any IGP.

The adjacency sub-TLV carries an Adjacency Type (1 parallel, 4 IPv4, 6 IPv6, 0 unnumbered), the Protocol, local and remote interface IDs, and the advertising and receiving node identifiers (a 32-bit OSPF Router ID or a 48-bit IS-IS System ID, depending on Protocol).

RFC 8287 also extends the Downstream Detailed Mapping TLV from RFC 8029 with two new Protocol values for label distribution: 5 for OSPF and 6 for IS-IS, alongside the existing Unknown, Static, BGP, LDP and RSVP-TE.
sections.eli5: Each stop on the list gets a little label that says what kind of stop it is and where to find it, so the checker knows what to look for.

sections.title: Building and Trimming the FEC Stack
sections.content:
For ping, the initiator MUST include FEC(s) for the destination segment, and MAY include FECs for some or all of the other segments it imposed.

For traceroute, the initiator MUST at first include FECs for all segments in the label stack. When an echo reply carries a FEC Stack Change TLV saying some original segments were popped, the initiator MAY remove the matching FECs from the next (TTL+1) request. If the reply has no such TLV, it MUST NOT remove any.

Who reports a pop? The node that advertised a Node Segment ID generates the FEC Stack Change sub-TLV for the POP, whether or not Penultimate Hop Popping (PHP) is enabled. For an Adjacency Segment ID, the node immediately downstream of the advertiser does so. Because PHP of a Node SID is like Implicit Null, implementations SHOULD use Implicit Null in those cases and for Adjacency SID PHP.

A Prefix SID can be advertised as an absolute value, an index or a range, and the initiator MUST derive the prefix it maps to. How the responder uses the sub-TLV for validation is a local implementation matter.
sections.eli5: As the traveler passes each stop, the stop crosses itself off the list, and the checker crosses it off its own copy only when told that happened.

sections.title: The Segment ID Check
sections.content:
RFC 8287 rewrites step 4 of the FEC validation in Section 4.4.1 of RFC 8029 and adds a step 4a for SR. If the label mapping for the FEC is Implicit Null, the FEC-status is set to 2. If it is the expected label, validation continues. Otherwise the return code is 10 ("Mapping for this FEC is not the given label at stack-depth").

In step 4a, a responder checks the sub-TLV at the current FEC stack depth. For IPv4 and IPv6 prefix SIDs it validates that the Node Segment ID is advertised for the prefix by the IGP named in the Protocol field (an unrecognized Protocol value is treated as 0). At label-stack depth 0 it also checks that the SID was advertised with the No-PHP flag clear. If no protocol associated with the incoming interface would have advertised that FEC type, it returns code 12 ("Protocol not associated with interface at FEC-stack-depth").

For the adjacency sub-TLV, failures give return code 35, newly assigned here ("Mapping for this FEC is not associated with the incoming interface"). For adjacency types 4 and 6 the responder checks that the Remote Interface ID matches the interface the packet arrived on, that the Receiving Node Identifier is its own IGP identifier, and that the SID is advertised by the Advertising Node Identifier in its local IGP database. For a parallel adjacency, the interface check is skipped.
sections.eli5: The router that gets the question looks in its own notebook and asks, "Did I really announce this stop, on this road?" If not, it says so with a numbered code.

sections.title: TTL Handling in Traceroute
sections.content:
Traceroute walks hop by hop by raising the TTL. Under the Uniform Model of RFC 3443 it can traverse every hop of the SR network. Under the Short Pipe Model, which the RFC calls one of the most commonly used, there is no TTL copy when the outer label is popped, so it may not.

A technique that MAY be used for Short Pipe: the initiator SHOULD set the TTL to 1 for the tunnel it wants to trace from, the TTL of all outer labels to the maximum value and the TTL of all inner labels to zero. The FEC Stack TLV, if included, should contain only the FECs for the inner-stacked tunnels. When one tunnel is done, the next is traced, and the end of a tunnel shows when the return code says the responder is an egress for the stack at depth 1. In this way the RFC 8029 procedures are applied recursively to a source-routed LSP.
sections.eli5: Each label in the stack has its own countdown clock. To check one leg at a time, you set the clock for the leg you care about to 1 and keep the others from ending the trip early.

sections.title: Coexisting With Non-SR Devices
sections.content:
Networks may mix SR-capable and non-SR-capable nodes, with SR and non-SR LSPs stitched together as with LDP and RSVP. The same RFC 8029 mechanism applies. If a responder has no FEC mapping for what the initiator sent, it returns code 4 ("Replying router has no mapping for the FEC at stack-depth"), as in RSVP and LDP interworking.

One specific gap: when an SR node assigns an Adjacency SID for a non-SR node, traceroute may fail. The non-SR node does not know the IGP-Adjacency Segment ID sub-TLV and may not reply with FEC Stack Change sub-TLVs, so nodes further downstream may reply with code 4.
sections.eli5: If one friend in the group does not know the new game, they cannot tell you the score, and the next friend may say, "I do not know that one either."

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The Security Considerations section is short: the document adds MPLS LSP Ping sub-TLVs and follows RFC 8029, so the security considerations of RFC 8029 apply and no additional challenges are introduced.

IANA assigned sub-types 34, 35 and 36 and created registries for the Protocol field in the Segment ID sub-TLV, the Adjacency Type, and the Protocol in the Downstream Detailed Mapping label stack sub-TLV. Values 0 to 250 are assigned by Standards Action, 251 to 254 are experimental and 255 is reserved. Return code 35 was also assigned.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is risky here, so the safety rules from the older document still apply.

fields.desc: The prefix the Segment ID is assigned to; trailing bits SHOULD be zero if shorter than 32 bits.
